issue.title: Move highlights_ref/clip_adapter.rs onto the shared subprocess_runner

task_type_fields.proposal:
Move `src/native/highlights_ref/clip_adapter.rs` onto the shared hardened runner `src/native/subprocess_runner.rs` (`subprocess_runner::run(&RunSpec { program, args, stdin, env, timeout, inherit_stdio: false })`), the way bob-cli-ea.4 already moved gkeep's adapter (`src/native/gkeep/adapter.rs:256`).

Root cause / current state: `clip_adapter.rs` still keeps its own private copy of the runner, namely `spawn_adapter` (~line 836, process_group(0) plus the ETXTBSY retry), `kill_adapter_tree` (~810), `kill_stragglers` (~801), `drain_pipe` (~871), and the hand-rolled stdin-writer / try_wait deadline loop in `run_request_with_hint` (~218-300). `subprocess_runner` provides the same process-group, timeout-kill, straggler-cleanup, ETXTBSY-retry, and stdin-error behavior and returns `RunOutput { status, stdout, stderr, timed_out, stdin_error }`.

Scope: replace the copy with one `subprocess_runner::run` call, then map `RunOutput` to the existing `AdapterFailure` messages byte-for-byte: the timeout message plus hint, "write the adapter request: …" when stdin failed with empty output, crash on exit code, and terminated by a signal. Delete the private helpers. web-clip / highlights-ref behavior and tests must stay byte-identical. Gate: `just check`.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The bob-cli-ea plan (phase gcal-auth, step 1) explicitly said to leave `highlights_ref/clip_adapter.rs`'s copy alone and file this follow-up. bob-cli-ea.4 note #1 proposed it. It is a code-health refactor of the web-clip path, which the gcal epic never touched.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-ea's plan deferred this extraction to a follow-up, and bob-cli-ea.4 note #1 proposed it. clip_adapter is now the last private copy of the hardened subprocess runner that gkeep and gcal share.

payload.description: Phase that extracted gkeep's runner into subprocess_runner and proposed this follow-up (note #1)
